text: This chapter covered six separate techniques: data parallelism, tensor and pipeline parallelism, ZeRO and FSDP sharding, activation checkpointing, and communication cost. None of them live in isolation in a real training job -- they show up together as settings in a single configuration file. This closing lesson walks through one real, complete DeepSpeed config line by line.

The per-GPU batch size and gradient accumulation steps give you the global batch size from lesson 28, made concrete. zero_optimization.stage sets the ZeRO sharding degree from lesson 30, with CPU offload for when even sharded memory isn't enough. activation_checkpointing turns on lesson 31's recompute-instead-of-store trick as a config block instead of hand-wrapped code. And bf16 enabled layers mixed precision on top of all of it.

Notice what's not in this file: no tensor-parallel degree, no pipeline-parallel degree. This config on its own assumes ZeRO-3 sharding within each data-parallel replica and ordinary data parallelism across replicas. Adding tensor or pipeline parallelism from lesson 29 means this config sits inside a larger launch configuration that sets those degrees separately, as a Megatron-DeepSpeed-level concern.

Here's the config itself -- micro batch size, accumulation steps, bf16 enabled, zero_optimization at stage 3 with CPU offload, and activation checkpointing with partition_activations. Every field here matches DeepSpeed's real documented config schema, nothing invented. Launch it with deepspeed --num_gpus=8, pointing at this file, and every GPU in the job reads the same configuration.

That closes Chapter 5. Parallelism gets a training job running across GPUs -- but running once isn't the same as running reliably for days or weeks at a time. Chapter 6, ML Systems for Training, covers what keeps a long run alive: checkpointing, fault tolerance, mixed precision in more depth, and observability for the duration of the run.
